chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a woman who made her slave girl permissible for me. He said: 'That is for you.' I said: 'For she was joking.' He said: 'What is there for you regarding what is in her heart? If you know that she was joking, then do not [take it as binding].'

key_terms.أَحَلَّتۡ: Made permissible (specifically referring to the act of offering a female slave for sexual relations)
key_terms.فَرَجَ: Private part / genitalia (here referring to the right of sexual access)
key_terms.فِي قَلۡبِهَا: In her heart (referring to internal intent)

ai.seo_question: Does a woman's offer of her slave girl for marriage or concubinage remain valid if she was joking?
ai.summary: In this narration from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the validity of *tamlik al-jariya* (granting sexual access to a slave girl) when the offerer is joking. He establishes that the external declaration (*zahir*) is sufficient for validity unless the recipient explicitly knows the internal intent (*batin*) of jest, thereby prioritizing the observable act in legal rulings. This highlights the Shia juristic principle that uncertainty of intent does not invalidate the contract unless that specific uncertainty is known to the other party.
